summary:
TEXNOLEAD - PROJECT SUMMARY
Lunar landing site selection and mission planning app for educational purposes. It uses NASA/JPL Horizons and NASA LOLA data. TexnoLead is an application developed as part of the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. TexnoLead helps users to analyse lunar south pole landing sites and mission planning windows. Users can select a landing site either from the available mapped locations or by entering custom coordinates. After selecting a landing site, users can enter a mission duration date range to analyse terrain effects, visibility of the Sun and Earth, and an idealised estimate of energy available from solar panels. While TexnoLead can help with preliminary planning and analysis of south pole landing sites, it does not validate landing sites or guarantee water ice presence. Its radio communications analysis also does not perform a full radio link budget.
details:
PROJECT DETAILS

1. WHAT DOES IT DO, AND HOW DOES IT WORK?

Given a date and location (selected from a list of sites of interest near the lunar south pole or by clicking on the map), this applet queries JPL Horizons for the azimuth and elevation angles of the Sun and Earth. These angles are compared to the local terrain skyline (from LOLA elevation data), and visibility of the Sun and Earth is shown, as well as their elevation angles relative to the terrain and an estimate of the solar energy profile. Users can compare multiple sites for the same time period. Use the long-term LOLA layers to view risk in the surrounding area. Download a report summarizing mission planning results. Note that the 90-, 180-, and 365-day time periods are not used to generate a risk plot for that entire time. Instead, these time periods are used to look for candidate mission start dates. The length of the mission itself (the time period for which results are shown) can be up to 31 days long.

2. WHAT BENEFITS DOES IT HAVE?

TexnoLead integrates several elements of mission planning into an interactive format that enables easy visualization and communication of the lunar environment. Locations and times can be compared, terrain occultations of the Sun and Earth can be understood, and solar illumination and direct-to-Earth visibility trade-offs can be examined. Together with graphs, source attribution, and clear identification of assumptions, TexnoLead makes conditions at the lunar south pole more accessible.

3. WHAT IS THE INTENDED IMPACT?

The tool is meant to provide an initial screening of potential landing sites and mission windows rather than replace the need for detailed engineering tailored to a particular mission. The results from the tool are not intended to be used to certify the safety of landing at a particular site. Provide lunar south pole exploration planning capability to a wider user community liks mission planners, educators, general public, etc. Point users toward potential questions that should be addressed through additional analyses.

4. WHAT TOOLS, CODING LANGUAGES, HARDWARE, AND SOFTWARE WERE USED?

Languages: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Python.

Python libraries: NumPy and Rasterio for geospatial raster analysis.

Web software: Leaflet for the interactive lunar map; SVG-based charts for the Sun and Earth telemetry.

5. HOW IS THE PROJECT CREATIVE?

Well our project calculates the effects of the local skyline (not just a flat horizon) on the visibility of (potentially partially obscured) Sun and Earth discs over time for user-selected locations on the Moon (with the ability to examine the terrain and PSR layer data in and around those locations, compare different locations, understand how the Sun and Earth screening metric is calculated, etc.) using an interactive map of the Moon.

6. WHAT FACTORS DID THE TEAM CONSIDER?

Factors considered by our team included power availability (Sun exposure), proximity to the terminator (visibility from Earth), slope and elevation of the site, availability of data, and the location of PSRs and potential landing sites (latitude and longitude). Temperatures and PSRs provided by the team were estimates. Horizons outputs are for a particular date and LOLA products are averages. PSRs (permanently shadowed regions) as defined in this application refer to locations that are in shadow according to the map products used.
